abstract: A first-party nsys capture of the v2c baseline in steady state, taken after the pre-tokenized token cache removed the dataloader bottleneck, so it measures what limits the run now rather than what limited it before. Command: nsys profile -t cuda,osrt -s none --delay 75 --duration 45 on an unmodified sealed run (/bin/bash launch.sh) on GPU 4. Totals over the window: 25.83s of GPU kernel time against 45s of wall, i.e. 57.4% busy; 102,337 kernel launches over ~179 optimizer steps, about 572 launches per step; 144.3ms of kernel time per step. Kernel time by class: GEMM (nvjet) 45.4% over 30,363 launches; FlashAttention 19.6% over 5,728; RMSNorm (Triton) 18.6% over 10,653; other elementwise Triton 8.1% over 32,071; softmax and cross-entropy 7.7% over 2,327. The two log_softmax/nll_loss kernels are the largest single kernels in the profile at 4.79ms and 4.28ms average, together about 9.1ms per optimizer step. Caveats that belong with the numbers: the host is shared and was at load ~325 with foreign tenants resident on other GPUs, and nsys itself inflates gaps -- observed step time rose from ~385ms unprofiled to ~480ms under the profiler with much higher variance (339-750ms). The idle fraction is therefore an upper bound on recoverable time, while the kernel-time shares are internally normalised and robust to both effects.

title: Nsight Systems steady-state GPU profile of the v2c baseline (45s window, H200, GPU 4)
